decision_log.scope_statement: Approved the hull surface-detail revision of the Alliance Pelagic battleship - the only asset this revision changes. The owner's words were "This looks good", after reviewing the revision against the approved hull at capital-detail, capital-close and tactical cameras plus native-pixel crops of the bow deck and the aft machinery.

revision.change: hull surface detail: raised deck plating with edge trenches, banded bow-crown armour with strakes and machinery wells, flank armour belt with dark gaps, machinery banks, vent banks, bridge-base window bands, drive housings, ram ribs, owner-colour prow chevron and deck centre stripe
revision.silhouette_change: length unchanged, beam grown: every detail element stands 0.5 to 4 world units proud of the surface it sits on, and at the hull's widest section - the armour belt, its dark plate gaps and the flank machinery banks at z -105 to -69 - that proud detail is the mesh's X extent, so the beam moves from 69.0 to 73.349998 and the mesh is 6.3 percent wider. The Y and Z extents are unchanged to the digit (Z -143.5 to 135.0), so the in-game length, which the renderer takes from the catalogue size policy on Z, is unchanged, and no collision or simulation field moves: radii come from the data files, not from the mesh.
revision.corrections: This record first said the revision changed no silhouette. That held for the length and not for the beam: the mesh outgrew the envelope declared for the previous revision, and the S02 extension-contract validator noticed it while PR #117 was being made to pass again against main. The extents above are measured from the two payloads rather than reasoned from the Z extent, and the artifact itself is unchanged - this is the record catching up with the file the owner approved, not a new revision.

decision_log.scope_statement: Approved the hull surface-detail revision of the Alliance escort (rebel_frigate) and the Alliance-owned (rebel) shipyard - the only two assets this revision changes, and the same two the authoring-ceiling decision s07-detail-budget-2026-10-16 was written for. The owner's words were "Models looking good approved", after reviewing the revision against the approved hulls at escort-close and yard-close with native-pixel crops of the frigate's flank and the yard's rails, at the shipped cameras, frozen view time and production default materials.

assets.change: hull surface detail: aft deck transverse frame bands and machinery wells, longitudinal deck strakes, deck-edge rail posts and feet, raised bow-crown armour bands and strakes, flank armour belt with dark inter-plate trenches, a second lower belt row, machinery banks, vent louvres, keel frame ribs, drive-casing machinery banks clipped to the beam, bridge-base window bands with a dark inset, owner-colour prow chevron

station surface detail: rail crown frame bands, plating panels, strakes and access hatches; rail flank armour belt, inter-plate trenches, machinery banks, vent banks and service pads down the outer face; gantry pedestal collars and gussets; slip guide-shoe contact plates and wear strips; crosshead machinery banks with radiator fins and frame lines; operations-tower window bands with a dark inset and machinery ledges; under-keel tie ribs

revision.silhouette_change: none - every element stands 0.4 to 3 world units proud of the surface it sits on; both payload bounding boxes are identical before and after (frigate 68.0 x 35.35 x 153.699997, shipyard 111.400002 x 56.400002 x 97.5), so the frigate's in-game length 96.180525 and the station's 110.0 radius are unchanged, and no collision or simulation field moves. The frigate's drive-casing detail is clipped to the +/-34 beam that already set the ship's widest point.
revision.shared_toolchain_change: The revision also raised the authoring ceiling (decision s07-detail-budget-2026-10-16), which moved the shared exporter tools/art/alliance_common.py, and added the shared detail module tools/art/hull_detail.py. Neither can change an approved byte: the battleship's .blend and runtime hashes in this file are untouched and validate-models still satisfies them. The live exporter binding of the earlier s06 entry is corrected to the current alliance_common.py hash for that reason; its decision_log entry keeps the hash as recorded at that approval, and nothing about the battleship's appearance changes.

This approves appearance only: it is not a landing, activation, merge, tag or release authorization for any of them, and it says nothing about the specimens of any other batch.
